slides.stem: Two similar cylindrical tanks have heights in the ratio $2:3$. If the smaller tank holds $80$ gallons, how many gallons does the larger tank hold?

slides.intro: Similar solids scale volume by the cube of the linear ratio.
slides.trapWhy: $120$ scales linearly. Volume cubes the ratio.

slides.title: Similar means one ratio, cubed for volume
slides.body:
Similar solids share a single linear ratio. Lengths scale by it, areas by its square, volumes by its cube.

Ask what the units measure: gallons are volume, so cube before you scale.
